content.text:
We need to resolve a March order. Starting region is either bay-of-ice or moat-cailin (the order assigned). The pending decision is resolve-single-march; we need to choose which starting region? The schema requires starting_region_id enum includes both options, we must pick one. The actionGuidance shows legalOrderRegions list contains two entries: bay-of-ice with unitIds [40]; moat-cailin with unitIds [48,55]. So we have to decide which order we are resolving now. Likely only one March order is pending, but we have two March orders placed (one on bay-of-ice, one on moat-cailin). The pending decision probably is for the first unresolved March order in turn order? The turn order is Iron Throne track: lannister first, then baratheon, greyjoy, martell, stark, tyrell. So Stark is 5th in order. In this phase, we resolve March orders in turn order: each player resolves one March order at a time, cycling. So earlier Lannister, Baratheon, Greyjoy, Martell have resolved their March orders already (maybe none?), now Stark resolves one March order. Which one? Since Stark has two March orders (bay-of-ice and moat-cailin). The order of resolution among own March orders? The rule: In turn order, each player resolves one of his March Orders on the game board. If a player has no such orders remaining, he skips. Keep cycling until no March orders remain. So Stark will resolve one March order now, and later will resolve the second when turn cycles again (another decision). So we need to choose which March order to resolve now. The actionGuidance lists both as legal starting regions. We must decide best move.

We need to consider capture gains and supply. Stark supply=1 (from earlier). So allowed armies per supply 1: According to supply table: supply 1 allows army sizes 3,2 (two armies: one up to 3, one up to 2). So at most two armies, each max size 3 and 2. Currently Stark units: at bay-of-ice: ship unit id 40 (type ship). At castle-black: 3 units (knight id2, footman id3, knight id47). At the-shivering-sea: ship id4. At winterfell: none (but garrison). At moat-cailin: knights id48 and 55 (2 knights). So we have armies: ship at bay-of-ice alone (size 1, not army). ship at shivering-sea alone. knights at moat-cailin count as army of size 2 (since two units same area). At castle-black three units = army size 3. That's within supply (two armies size <=3 and <=2). Good.

Now moving units could change armies count/size. Must stay within supply after moves.

Potential moves:

- From bay-of-ice: reachable regions per actionGuidance: port-of-winterfell (type port) castleAreasGainedIfCaptured 0, no combat, controller "stark". Actually port-of-winterfell is owned by Stark (controlPowerToken maybe?) It shows controller "stark". So moving ship into port-of-winterfell would not trigger combat; it's a port, you can have ships there, but you must have an order placed there (there is a defense order on port-of-winterfell? Wait there is a defense order on port-of-winterfell? In board list, port-of-winterfell has no order. Actually earlier we placed a March order on port-of-winterfell (orderId 2 March +0). That has been resolved. Now that order is resolved and the ship moved? Wait the March order on port-of-winterfell was resolved earlier (Round 9). The ship moved from port-of-winterfell to bay-of-ice. So now port-of-winterfell is empty of units. It has no order now (since that March order resolved). So moving ship into port-of-winterfell is allowed as a destination (but need to have a port and be its owner? Port ownership is determined by land area control. The land area for port-of-winterfell is winterfell (home). Stark controls winterfell, so Stark can move ship into port-of-winterfell.

- Also bay-of-ice can move to sunset-sea (sea) which has controller Greyjoy, triggers combat (since enemy ship present? Actually sunset-sea currently has one Greyjoy ship (id44) per board. So moving Stark ship into sunset-sea would trigger combat (one destination can trigger combat). Could attack that ship. Need to consider support around sunset-sea. Check neighbours: Let’s use tool check_neighbours on sunset-sea.

So adjacent sea areas to sunset-sea: bay-of-ice, flints-finger, ironmans-bay (Greyjoy), searoad-marches, the-golden-sound, west-summer-sea. Only ironmans-bay has enemy ships. But combat triggers when moving into area that contains enemy units (ships). So moving into sunset-sea will encounter a Greyjoy ship? Actually sunset-sea currently has a Greyjoy ship (id44). Wait the board entry "sunset-sea" shows units: [{ "allegiance":"greyjoy","id":44,"type":"ship"}]. So moving Stark ship from bay-of-ice into sunset-sea will engage that ship. That's combat between ship vs ship. Ships have combat strength 1 each. Attack will have March -1 modifier (from bay-of-ice order) and maybe Defense order on sunset-sea? There is no order on sunset-sea (Consolidate Power). No defense. So combat strength: attacker gets 1 (ship) + March -1 = 0? Actually March -1 gives -1. So attacker strength = 0. Defender gets 1. No support (likely). So Stark would lose. Might be undesirable.

Alternatively moving to port-of-winterfell: no combat, just relocate ship. That would keep ship in home port. Could later be used for transport? Probably good.

Now consider moat-cailin.

From moat-cailin reachable: greywater-watch (land, no castle), seagard (land, castleLevel=2 stronghold), the-twins (land), white-harbor (land castleLevel=1), winterfell (castleLevel=2, already Stark). No combat in any because no enemy units present. Capturing seagard or white-harbor would gain castle areas (seagard stronghold=2 castle area? Actually stronghold counts as one castle area for victory points, same as castle). The actionGuidance says seagard castleLevel=2, castleAreasGainedIfCaptured=1. Good. Similarly white-harbor has castleLevel=1, gives 1.

Goal: we need to preserve Moat Cailin's castle contribution (currently 1 castle area). If we move all units out of Moat Cailin, we lose that castle area unless we leave a power token (cannot). So we must leave at least one unit there to keep castle. So moving both knights would vacate and lose castle. So we can move only one knight, keep the other. Or we could move none (skip). However moving a knight to seagard captures a stronghold, gaining a castle area, net effect: lose moat cailin castle (1) but gain seagard stronghold (1) = net 0. But also we keep one unit at moat cailin to preserve? Actually if we move one knight, the other remains, so Moat Cailin still occupied, so we keep castle. Then we capture seagard stronghold gaining +1, net +1 castle area. That improves victory points.

But need supply: moving one knight to seagard results in knights distribution: moat cailin now has 1 knight (army size 1 not army). Castle Black still army size 3. Ship at bay-of-ice + ship at shivering sea + maybe ship moved later. So armies: castle-black (size 3) counts as army. moat cailin single knight not army. ship units singles not armies. So we have only one army size 3, within supply (allowed). Good.

We also could move both knights to seagard or white-harbor, but then Moat Cailin empty => lose castle area. Might be okay if we also capture stronghold (maybe we can also capture white-harbor also stronghold). But only one destination may trigger combat (none). Could we split: one knight to seagard, one to white-harbor? That would capture two castles (gain +2) but lose Moat Cailin castle (-1). Net +1. Supply: after moving both knights, Moat Cailin becomes empty (no units), we cannot leave power token, so we lose castle. The knights would be in separate lands, each single unit (not armies). So total armies: castle-black (size3). Others single units not count. So still ok.

But can we move both knights as separate groups? Moves list can have up to 2 groups. The actionGuidance says supplySafeUnitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone includes groupings for each unit alone or both together. So moving both knights together to same destination is also allowed (group size 2) but then Moat Cailin empty -> lose castle. Might still be okay.

We need to decide best outcome in terms of victory points and future. Gaining stronghold seagard or white-harbor good. Also we have a ship at bay-of-ice. Perhaps we also want to move that ship somewhere safe? Port-of-winterfell maybe. That does not affect castles. Could also consider moving ship to port-of-winterfell to consolidate fleet for transport later, maybe to attack or defend.

Which move should we prioritize? Castle points: Currently Stark controls 2 castles (castle-black and winterfell) + 1 stronghold (Moat Cailin) = total castle areas =2 (castle) + stronghold counts as one, so 3? Wait controlledCastleAreas field is 2 (maybe only counting castle areas, not strongholds?). The strategic overview said controlledCastleAreas 2; castle and stronghold each count as ONE. Stark has winterfell (castle) and castle-black (castle) => 2. Moat Cailin stronghold not counted? maybe separate count for strongholds not shown. Anyway we need more.

Capturing seagard stronghold would increase castle areas to 3 (including winterfell, castle-black, seagard) while still retaining Moat Cailin if we leave a knight. That would be +1. Good.

We also have ship in bay-of-ice. Could we move ship to port-of-winterfell (no combat) and keep ship for future transport? That won't affect castle count. Might be beneficial for defending winterfell maybe.

But we can only resolve one March order now. Which should we prioritize? The decision says "compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack." There is no combat if we move to seagard etc.

Thus likely best is to resolve moat-cailin order, moving one knight to seagard (gain one castle area) and keep the other to preserve Moat Cailin. That yields net +1 castle area without combat.

But we also could consider moving both knights to seagard (gain +1) but lose Moat Cailin castle (-1) net 0. Not as good.

Alternatively move one knight to white-harbor (castle) also +1 net +0 if we keep one knight. We could choose either seagard or white-harbor. Which is better strategically? Seagard is stronghold near Greyjoy area and close to ship routes? White-harbor is near the sea, also maybe useful later. No immediate difference.

Check support around seagard: Evaluate neighbours support maybe from Greyjoy? Let's check neighbours of seagard.{"area":"seagard"}

Seagard currently not controlled by any house (owner null) and no enemy units. Capturing it likely no combat. No support needed.

White-harbor?{"area":"white-harbor"}

actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
